purpose: Professional GIS, 3D terrain, and game-engine toolchain baseline for war-animation-lab-oss. Tactical Terrain Studio should orchestrate and audit these tools instead of replacing them.

defaultProductionPolicy.summary: Future war animations should be planned as game-engine-capable productions by default. React/MapLibre remains useful as a review UI, lightweight interactive front end, or fallback, but the production map/terrain/unit pipeline should be designed so it can move into Unreal/Unity/Godot or a Web 3D engine without being rebuilt from scratch.
minimumImplications: Every new battle needs a terrain/data package before animation implementation.
Unit movement should be authored as engine-ready tracks with per-unit transforms, facing, formation membership, visibility, and contact/collision metadata.
Camera plans should be expressed as cinematic shots and tactical review cameras, not only map zoom numbers.
Disk cache, derived data, source assets, exported renders, and tile caches must be budgeted before production starts.

tools.name: OpenTopography Global Datasets API
tools.role: Fetch source DEMs such as SRTM GL1/GL3, NASADEM, ALOS World 3D, Copernicus COP30/COP90, and bathymetry datasets.
tools.fit: Primary automated DEM acquisition path when API key and license constraints are acceptable.

tools.name: Copernicus DEM GLO-30/GLO-90
tools.role: Global DSM source with edited water bodies and river consistency.
tools.fit: Preferred modern global terrain source for many battlefields, with source notes that it is DSM rather than bare-earth DTM.

tools.name: NASA SRTM
tools.role: Near-global elevation reference covering most land surfaces.
tools.fit: Fallback or cross-check source when Copernicus/OpenTopography access is incomplete.

tools.name: Natural Earth
tools.role: Public-domain vector/raster reference layers at 1:10m, 1:50m, and 1:110m scales.
tools.fit: Campaign/regional maps; not sufficient alone for tactical battlefields.

tiers.name: GIS Authoring, Georeferencing, and Terrain Derivatives

tools.name: QGIS
tools.role: Desktop GIS for layer inspection, CRS control, georeferencing, clipping, digitizing, terrain analysis, and QA.
tools.fit: Mandatory manual/professional workbench before hard battles are animated.

tools.name: GDAL
tools.role: CLI/library for raster/vector translation, warping, hillshade, slope, aspect, contour, and tile preparation.
tools.fit: Mandatory reproducible processing layer behind QGIS work.

tools.name: Qgis2threejs
tools.role: QGIS plugin for visualizing DEM and vector data in 3D and exporting web/3D assets.
tools.fit: Useful for offline terrain look-dev and reference exports; not the default runtime renderer.

tools.name: BlenderGIS
tools.role: Blender bridge for importing GIS vectors, rasters, GeoTIFF DEMs, and OSM data into 3D scenes.
tools.fit: Optional cinematic terrain/modeling pipeline when MapLibre terrain is not visually strong enough.

tools.name: Tippecanoe
tools.role: Build vector tilesets from GeoJSON, FlatGeobuf, or CSV features.
tools.fit: Primary path for turning battle-specific historical layers into vector tiles when GeoJSON becomes heavy.

tools.name: PMTiles / Protomaps
tools.role: Single-file tiled archive suitable for static hosting with HTTP range requests.
tools.fit: Preferred local/static artifact format for battle map packages.

tools.name: Martin
tools.role: Rust tile server for PostGIS, PMTiles, and MBTiles sources.
tools.fit: Local or production tile serving when multiple sources need to be combined dynamically.

tools.name: tilemaker
tools.role: Generate OpenStreetMap vector tiles from .osm.pbf extracts without a database.
tools.fit: Optional OSM-derived context layer pipeline, not battle-specific historical reconstruction.

tools.name: MapTiler Terrain RGB / Engine
tools.role: DEM-to-RGB terrain tile workflow and hosted/on-prem terrain datasets.
tools.fit: Commercial/professional alternative for terrain RGB tiles when local GDAL tiling is too weak.

tools.name: MapLibre GL JS
tools.role: Open WebGL map renderer with raster-dem terrain and geographic overlay support.
tools.fit: Default runtime for current React war animations.

tools.name: CesiumJS
tools.role: 3D globe/terrain/3D Tiles runtime with terrain providers and quantized-mesh terrain.
tools.fit: Evaluation candidate for high-relief 3D scenes, broad theaters, or cinematic flythroughs.

tools.name: deck.gl TerrainLayer and TerrainExtension
tools.role: GPU terrain mesh reconstruction from height maps and draping of data over terrain.
tools.fit: Evaluation candidate for custom WebGL layer composition and analytical overlays.

tools.name: MapLibre GL JS custom Three.js layer
tools.role: Place Three.js GLTF/mesh objects on MapLibre terrain while preserving geographic camera alignment.
tools.fit: Best bridge when the app must remain React/Web/MapLibre but needs real 3D unit models, terrain-height placement, and better lighting than SVG overlays.

tools.name: Three.js
tools.role: General-purpose WebGL 3D engine with cameras, animation mixers, instancing, materials, lighting, and custom terrain meshes.
tools.fit: Best for self-contained tactical diorama scenes and custom unit animation when geospatial streaming is not the dominant problem.

tools.name: Babylon.js
tools.role: Web 3D engine with heightmap ground, thin instances, physics integrations, animation tooling, and crowd/navigation extensions.
tools.fit: Good candidate for web-based large unit counts, animated formations, and more game-like battle scenes without leaving the browser.

tools.name: deck.gl TerrainLayer / TripsLayer / PathLayer
tools.role: GPU map visualization layers for terrain meshes, animated tracks, and meter-aware paths.
tools.fit: Strong for analytical animated geospatial layers; weaker for full cinematic unit-model battles.

tools.name: Unreal Engine + Cesium for Unreal
tools.role: High-end 3D battlefield simulation, cinematic cameras, landscape/lighting, Nanite/Lumen-style scene fidelity, and streamed geospatial 3D Tiles terrain.
tools.fit: Best candidate when a battle needs professional 3D terrain, cinematic rendering, complex camera blocking, physics/collision, or offline video-grade output.

tools.name: Unreal Engine World Partition / Landscape / Sequencer
tools.role: Large terrain streaming, open-world landscape management, and cinematic keyframe sequencing.
tools.fit: Use when the battlefield becomes a full 3D scene rather than an interactive web map.

tools.name: Unity Terrain + DOTS/ECS + Timeline
tools.role: Real-time 3D terrain, scalable entity processing, and timeline-based animation production.
tools.fit: Candidate for cross-platform interactive simulations with many independently controlled units, if Unity build/export workflow is acceptable.

tools.name: Godot 3D + NavigationAgent3D
tools.role: Open-source 3D scenes, navigation/pathfinding, and scriptable animation.
tools.fit: Open-source option for lighter game-engine prototypes; terrain/geospatial pipeline is less mature than Unreal/Cesium for professional map work.

tools.name: OGC 3D Tiles
tools.role: Open standard for streaming massive heterogeneous 3D geospatial datasets.
tools.fit: Data interchange target when scenes need to move between CesiumJS, Cesium for Unreal, and other 3D geospatial renderers.

tools.name: milsymbol
tools.role: JavaScript generator for MIL-STD-2525 and STANAG APP-6 symbols.
tools.fit: Reference for tactical graphic grammar and optional modern-war overlays; ancient unit markers still need era-specific illustrations.

tools.name: ArcGIS Military Dictionary Styles
tools.role: Dictionary-rendered APP-6 and MIL-STD-2525 symbol standards in ArcGIS.
tools.fit: Professional reference for standards coverage, not a direct dependency for this React app.

baselinePipeline: Define battle AOI, historical uncertainty, and tactical feature list.
Fetch DEM/source reference data through OpenTopography/Copernicus/SRTM and record license/source notes.
Use QGIS to georeference historical maps and digitize battlefield features with GCP evidence.
Use GDAL to warp/clip DEM, generate hillshade/slope/contours, and export reproducible derivatives.
Package historical features as GeoJSON first; promote to Tippecanoe/PMTiles/Martin when feature volume or performance requires it.

Render in MapLibre by default for map-first tactical animations; evaluate MapLibre+Three, CesiumJS, deck.gl, Babylon.js, or Three.js when SVG overlays cannot carry unit depth, terrain-height placement, lighting, or animated models.

Escalate to Unreal/Cesium or Unity/Godot only when the scene needs professional cinematic terrain, real 3D camera blocking, collision/physics/navigation, or offline video-grade rendering beyond what a web map can responsibly provide.
Run Tactical Terrain Studio audits for camera envelope, unit density, route handoffs, feature crossings, closed pockets, winner-remains-on-field, and screenshot evidence.
